case_number: CRL. A. NO. 740 OF 2022 @ SLP (CRL.) NO.3564 OF 2022

parties.respondent: The State of Madhya Pradesh and Another

summary: Appeal against bail granted to accused in case involving allegations of rape under IPC Section 376(2)(n) and criminal intimidation under Section 506. Accused allegedly induced physical relationship by false promise of marriage, resulted in pregnancy and forced abortion. Bail granted by High Court despite prior rejections of anticipatory bail. Appellant challenged bail citing threat, witness tampering, and influential status of accused. High Court did not record reasons for bail. Prosecution highlighted accused's criminal antecedents and material evidence including photos symbolizing marriage. Respondent claimed consensual relationship and delay in FIR; alleged blackmail. State opposed bail, citing multiple criminal cases against accused and family. Supreme Court emphasized need for judicial application of mind in bail decisions, considering nature of accusation, severity of punishment, evidence, threat to complainant, and prima facie case.
legal_provisions_cited: Ram Govind Upadhyay v. Sudarshan Singh
Prahlad Singh Bhati v. NCT, Delhi
Chaman Lal v. State of U.P.
final_judgment: Leave granted. Appeal allowed. Bail granted by High Court set aside. Matter remanded to High Court for fresh hearing on bail application with proper application of judicial mind and recording of reasons.
